He consecrates it with: "Thou art a spade; thou art a woman" (VS 1.29). With the formula: "Here I cut off the neck of the Rakṣas," he traces around the holes for the sacrificial posts (*upa-ra-vāḥ*) on the south side of the *maṇḍapa*, moving clockwise, each measuring a span (*prādeśa*) in depth, so as to leave room for the post-hole which is to be dug arm-deep. In front of the holes for the sacrificial posts, he prepares a square mound (*khara*) arm-deep and high enough to serve as a support, using earth from the holes. Having sprinkled it with water, he fills it with sand.

He encourages [the sacrificer] with the words, "Thou art great, O great one, worthy of praise. He digs in successive order. With the words, "Thou art a sovereign ruler," he throws up the first [earth]; with "Thou art a self-ruler," the second; with "Thou art a far-shining ruler," the third; and with "Thou art a continuous ruler," the fourth. Having cleared the space below with the words, "Thou art great, O great one, worthy of praise," he throws up all [the earth] together with the words, "Thou art a universal ruler. He casts the thrown-up earth onto the rubbish-heap (utkara). With the words, "Touch them together," he touches the Uparava holes. The Adhvaryu touches the southern one of the two front holes, and the other [priest] touches the northern one of the two rear holes.

The sacrificer asks, "What is here? The Adhvaryu says, "A blessing. The sacrificer replies, "May that be for us both. Following the response, the Adhvaryu erects the southern [post], and the sacrificer the northern one. The Adhvaryu asks, "What is here? The Adhvaryu says, "A blessing. The sacrificer says, "May that be mine. To the north, at the midpoint between the *sadas* and the *havirdhāna*, he erects the Āgnīdhra shed, which has four pillars, a door facing south, and its beams pointing east.

Half of it is within the altar and half is outside the altar. From the upper edge of the altar, he establishes the *sadas* at a distance of three *prakramas* or in an unlimited space from the western end of the altar; it is nine *aratnis* long from east to west and twenty-seven *aratnis* across. In its middle, to the south of the *pṛṣṭhyā* line, he digs a pit for the *audumbara* post, measuring one *prakrama*, just as the pit for the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) is prepared, up to the point of strewing. While the *audumbara* post, which is as tall as the sacrificer, is being raised, the *udgātṛ* takes hold of it. He raises it with the verse: "O Lord of the Forest, rise up! (VS 6.22).

16. "May the Marut strike you down," saying this, he places [the earth] toward the east of the ear. 17. "I pile around you, the winner of the Brahman, the winner of the Kṣatra," saying this, he piles it around with clods of earth. 18. "May the Brahman be firm, may the Kṣatra be firm," saying this, the consecrated sacrificer strokes [the altar] clockwise with the consecration-staff. 19. He sprinkles water around [it]. 20. Having placed gold between his two ears, he makes an offering over [the altar] with the formula, "With ghee, fill heaven and earth. 21. He lets it flow down to the root. 22. "The exhilaration is upward-pointing, auspicious, and within me."

He measures [the Audumbarī post]. (22) The Audumbarī is the tallest among the pillars; the others are shorter, and the last one is the shortest. (23) There are nine roof-coverings: with the tips turned upward in the Agniṣṭoma, fifteen in the Ukthya, seventeen in the Atirātra, twenty-one in the Sattras and Ahīnas, and eleven in the Ṣoḍaśin and the Vājapeya. (24) With the formula, "The shadow of all people art thou," he places the middle roof-covering on the Audumbarī. Having placed the eastern one, he places the western one.

He fastens the southern [loops] and draws up the northern ones. (25) With the verse, "O lover of songs, may our songs encompass thee," he encloses [the shed]. (26) Beginning with the formula, "For Indra thee," he mutters it at the junction of the middle and the western [walls]. (27) With the formula, "Thou art the needle of Indra," he sews [the seams]. (28) With the formula, "Thou art the fixed point of Indra," he makes the first knot. (29) He should sew right through to the end. (30) Having sewn the other joints, he sews the door-posts. (31) Having consecrated the completed structure with the formula, "Thou belongest to Indra; for Indra thee," [he prepares] the sprinkling waters.

Having consecrated them with the formula, "I sprinkle you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu," he sprinkles the *uparavas*. (32) With the formula, "I pour water upon you, the Rakṣas-slayer, the Valaga-slayer," he pours water upon each one individually. (33) With the formula, "I spread grass upon you, the Rakṣas-slayer, the Valaga-slayer," he spreads *darbha* grass upon each one individually. (34) Upon two *audumbara* pressing-boards, which are cut level together at the back and front and shaped like a wheel-rim, [he places them] measuring a cubit in height.

35. He strikes [the ground] two finger-breadths behind [the axle]. 36. Having moved aside, he places [two bricks] between the two shafts with the formula, "I place you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the Valaga-slayers. 37. With the formula, "I enclose you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the Valaga-slayers," he encloses them with earth using the *pām̐su* formulas. 38. He makes the pressing-surface upon the skin of the *adhivicayana*. 39. Having moved aside and having spread [a hide] between the two pressing-boards with the formula, "I spread you, the Rakṣas-slayer, the Valaga-slayer," he fastens the hair-side upwards so that the hairs are joined together.

To the south of the Āgnīdhra’s shed, he makes the mark for the Āgnīdhrīya hearth: (1) having dug up the earth and sprinkled it with water, he pours down clods from the Cātvāla pit; (2) having leveled them and sprinkled them with water, he causes them to shine by covering them with sand; (3) in this same manner he pours down the Dhiṣṇya hearths, six of which are within the Sadas.

At the location of the *pṛṣṭhyā* line, at a distance of one cubit from the western door, he establishes the *hotrīya* hearth; to the south, the *maitrāvaruṇīya* hearth, so that the *audumbarī* post shall lie exactly midway between these two. To the north, at a distance of one cubit from each other, he establishes the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsīya*, the *potrīya*, the *neṣṭrīya*, and the *achāvākya* hearths. At a distance from the *hotrīya* equal to that between the *hotrīya* and the *āgnīdhrīya*, he establishes the *mārjālīya* hearth to the south-east. To the south of the *cātvāla* pit, within the *antarvedi* area, he spreads the sacrificial grass. To the north of the *cātvāla* pit, he marks the site for the *śāmitra* fire.

Having lifted [the fire] and sprinkled [water], the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer, walking around [the altar] in the same direction, worship the *dhiṣṇya* hearths with the formulas beginning with "Vibhū asi pravāhaṇaḥ" according to the order in which they were established, and with those beginning with "Samrāj asi" for the Āhavanīya. Standing between the *āstāva* and within the altar, they worship the *cātvāla*, the *śāmitra*, the *sadas*, the Audumbarī post, the *brahmaloka*, and having circumambulated the Āgnīdhrīya to the north, they worship the Śālāmukhīya, the Gārhapatya, and the Dakṣiṇāgni.

The phrase "with the fierce troop" is to be supplied everywhere [in the subsequent formulas]. (8) Between the *tīrtha* and the *cātvāla*, and between the *āgnīdhra* and the *āgnīdhrīya*, there is a path for movement. (9) One should not pass between the *dhiṣṇya* hearths. If the Adhvaryu should pass beyond the *dhiṣṇyas* facing westward, he should recite the verse addressed to Indra (*aindrī*). (10) Between the *āgnīdhra* and the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, there is a passage for moving eastward. (11) They strew the altar according to the requirements of the ritual steps, shaking the earth layer by layer, either without covering the *dhiṣṇyas*, the *khara*, the *uparavas*, and the *uttaravedi*. (12) Having given half of the *vrata* milk, [he moves] to the north.

He places the fuel and the sacrificial grass for the Āhavanīya fire. The Adhvaryu and the sacrificer wash their hands. Having placed the fire for the procession at the Śālāmukhīya fire, he arranges the vessels pertaining to the animal sacrifice on the northern part of the altar, placing the *pracaraṇī* ladle to the south of the *sruva* spoon.

Its first cleaning is done silently. 15. [The procedure] is established up to the taking of the clarified butter (ājya). 16. He takes four portions of clarified butter mixed with speckled butter (pṛṣadājya). 17. He places the King (Soma) on the lap of the Brahman or that of the sacrificer. 18. Having led the wife forward by the path used by the initiated, saying, "Let the wife of the Brahman go forward; let her sit upon the altar with splendor," he makes her sit behind the sacrificer, saying, "And I, following you, shall enter my own world here. 19. Having taken four portions [of butter], [he offers] to Agni and Soma.

He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse with the words, "Recite for the two being led forward. (20) When it has been recited three times, he lifts up the implements for the leading forward of the fire. (21) The Adhvaryu hands them over to the Āgnīdhra; then, with a cloth having its fringe toward the east, they cover the limbs and the sacrificer. (22) Men take hold of the sacrificer from behind, and women take hold of the wife. (23) Having brought the fringe together at the handle of the offering-ladle, he offers with the verse, "O Soma, you [offer] to those who cause bodily harm... He offers a second oblation with the verse beginning, "The swift one, enjoying... (24) From this point onward, this [fire] becomes the Gārhapatya.

He scatters half a foot-measure of cold ashes over it. 25 They lead Agni in front. Behind him, in his lap, they lead the King [Soma] immediately after; following him, they lead the clarified butter, the throne-seat (*āsandī*), the pressing-stones (*grāvan*), the Vāyavya cups, the *droṇakalaśa* vessel, and the goat dedicated to Agni-Soma. 26 They go to the north of the *sadas*. 27 Having placed the fire on the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, he makes an offering with the formula, "O Agni, lead [us]. 28 He sets down the sacrificial vessels in the *āgnīdhra*; he fastens the throne-seat, the pressing-stones, the Vāyavya cups, the *droṇakalaśa*, and the goat. 29 The Brahman priest...

Taking the king (Soma), he stands behind the two *havirdhāna* sheds. Having offered oblations of clarified butter into the *āhavanīya* fire at the edge of the *uttaravedi* with the mantra, "O Viṣṇu, stride out widely," and having caused [the sacrificer] to drink the first portions, he spreads the single-layered sacrificial grass (*barhis*) behind the *uttaravedi*. The procedure for the placing of the clarified butters is established. The sacrificer enters by the eastern door with the mantra, "Thus, do thou praise."

The Adhvaryu priest carries the King Soma across [the altar] with the formula: "Go through the wide atmosphere" (33). Having stepped forward toward the southern shoulder, he spreads a black antelope skin upon the front part of the seat with the formula: "Thou art the skin of Aditi" (34). He places the King Soma upon it with the formula: "Sit upon the seat of Aditi" (35). The Adhvaryu mutters: "O God Savitṛ, this is thy Soma" (36), and the sacrificer mutters: "O God Soma, do thou [protect] that [of ours]" (36). Having said, "Here I [dismiss] men" (37), he turns back. He pays homage with the formula: "Homage to the gods" (38), and [releases himself] from the noose of Varuṇa with the formula: "From the noose of Varuṇa... (38).

He creeps out (39). He gazes at the fire or the sun, thinking, "May my voice be manifested" (40). He places a fuel-stick on the fire with the formula: "O Agni, lord of vows, that body of yours which was in me—let it be in you" (41). He mutters: "O Agni, lord of vows, that body of mine which was in you—let it be in me" (42). With the formula, "Again for us, O lord of vows," he releases his vows (43). He sits upon a black antelope skin. He should scratch himself with a Yajus-formula.

The wife shall eat the *haviṣya* (the sacrificial food), and the sacrificer shall eat the remnants of the *havis*. 44. Having passed between the two *havirdhāna* sheds and to the south of the handles of the offering-ladles, another sits down behind the *brahmán*; this is the path of movement. 45.

The Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula, the introductory rite for the animal sacrifice (paśukī), and the giving of the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) shall be omitted in those rites that are subordinate members [of the Soma sacrifice]. 1. If the consecrated sacrificer should die before the purchase [of the Soma], one should take the *sruva* ladle and the two churning sticks (*araṇī*), churn fire at the base of the sacrificial post (*yūpa*), and offer the oblation to the post (*yūpāhuti*). 2. If [he dies] after the purchase [of the Soma], having offered in the *āhavanīya* fire, the rite is completed starting from the pit for the post up to the preliminary dedication (*upākaraṇa*). 3. If [he dies] after the purchase, having offered in the *āhavanīya* fire, the rite is completed starting from the pit for the post up to the preliminary dedication. 4. He dedicates the goat intended for Agni and Soma (*agnīṣomīya*). 5. The rite is completed up to the invocation of the ancestral priests (*pravara*). 6. Once the *pravara* has been invoked...

He hands the consecration-staff to the Maitrāvaruṇa. 7. This is established up to the offering of the omentum. 8. When the omentum has been offered, having performed the purification at the *cātvāla* pit, he issues the command: "O Subrahmaṇya, invoke the Subrahmaṇyā!"

He invokes the Subrahmaṇyā formula with the *pitāputrīyā* verses. (9) He does not prepare the heart-spit at the Agniṣomīya sacrifice, nor at the Savanīya. (10) He does not throw the wooden chip (*svaru*) into the fire. (11) A path should not pass between the water and the sacrificial ground. (12) Having gone out before sunset, he takes up the Vasatīvarī waters. (13) Standing against the current of flowing waters, he dips the jar against the current with the formula, "These waters are rich in oblation," covering it at the junction of shadow and sunlight with either Darbha grass or his hand. (14) [With the formula: "Of Agni, whose house is secure..."

"I set it down in the assembly hall," [saying this], he sets it down behind the *śālāmukhīya* fire (15). If the sun has already set, he should take [the Soma] from the jar of one who has performed the *Soma* sacrifice (16). If he cannot find one who has performed the *Soma* sacrifice, there should be gold in his hand; they should hold the fire above him, and then he may take [the Soma] (17). Whatever he intends to give as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), he should give that as a choice gift to the *adhvaryu* (18). From the animal-cake offering (*paśupuroḍāśa*) onwards, the ritual is established until the *iḍā* of the animal sacrifice (19). Having carried [the portions] past the *havirdhāna*, the *ārjālīya*, and the *maitrāvaruṇīya* fires to the south, [he gives them] to the *hotṛ*.

He offers the *iḍā* of the animal victim (20). It is established for the *upayaj* offerings (21). The *āgnīdhra* priest pours out embers from the *śāmitra* fire onto the *hotṛ’s* hearth (22). He carries the rectum and the tail along the path of the *iḍā* (23). It is established up to the portions of the *saṃsrāva* (24). He takes up all the offering-spoons (25). At night, the sacrifice concludes with the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings (26). He binds together the sacrificial fuel (*idhma*) and the grass (*barhis*) used for the animal sacrifice (27). They milk the cow that provides the *vratadugh* (vow-milk) for the sacrificer for the *āśira* mixture; they milk the one belonging to the wife for the *payasyā* curd-offering to Mitra and Varuṇa.

That [milk] which belongs to the *pravargya* rite, he should set aside for the *dadhigharma*; having separated the milk, he should set it aside for the *dadhighraha*. The boiled and cooled [milk] is for the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup. Two pieces of gold are for the *śukra* cup. Barley meal is for the *manthin* cup. The two types of curds—the heated and cooled *ātaṅkyas*—are for the *ādityagraha* cup. Parched grains (*dhānās*) are for the *hāriyojana* cup. He causes the sacrificial vessels to be placed in the *āgnīdhra* shed. While staying awake there, the sacrificer observes the fast; the wife does so before the *vamiśa* [rite]. At night, he carries around the *vasatīvarī* waters.

They should not exclude one who has not been initiated (adīkṣita). The sacrificer and his wife should stand within the altar (antarvedi). Having entered by the eastern door, he takes up the Vasatīvarī waters. Having passed to the west of the sacrificial ground (vihāra), crossed to the south, and exited by the eastern door, he goes to the south of the Sadas, the Mārjālīya, and the Havirdhāna sheds; then, saying, "O you who belong to the portion of Indra and Agni," he places them on the southern corner of the northern altar (uttaravedi-śroṇi).

Having returned by the same way he came, having gone out by the eastern door, and having proceeded along the north of the *sadas*, the *āgnīdhra* shed, and the *havirdhāna* sheds, he deposits [the vessels] on the northern corner of the northern *uttaravedi* with the formula, "Ye are the portions of Mitra and Varuṇa"; [he deposits them] at the *āgnīdhra* fire-altar with the formula, "Of all the gods. He appends the phrase "desiring favor" (*sumnāyuvaḥ*) everywhere. 34. He issues the command, "O Subrahmaṇya, invoke the Subrahmaṇyā! He invokes the Subrahmaṇyā belonging to the father and son. 35.
Thus ends the second chapter in the *Mānava Sūtra* concerning the Agniṣṭoma.

He attends upon the *sadas* with a verse addressed to Indra as it dawns, the *āgnīdhra* shed with one addressed to Agni, and the *havirdhāna* shed with one addressed to Viṣṇu. He offers an oblation on the *āgnīdhrīya* fire with the formula: "Protect me from the mantra in the mouth, and from any curse whatsoever. To the north of the *āhavanīya* fire, he places the fuel and the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). The Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ wash their hands. Behind the *āgnīdhrīya*, he sets out the vessels for the animal sacrifice; those for the Soma-pressing are set out to the east.

From the *sruva* ladle, he takes the *pracaraṇī* offering-ladle; its first cleansing is performed silently. With the verse, "O Agni, do thou ferry us across," he worships the ladles. The procedure from the taking of the portions of clarified butter (*ājyagraha*) is established. Just as on the previous day at the *Āgnīdhrīya* fire, there is the cleansing of the ladles and the taking of the portions of clarified butter. They carry the clarified butter forward as far as the *uttaravedi* altar. From the raising [of the ladles] until the spreading of the grass, the procedure is established. Half of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is for the *prastara*; the *idhma-prastara* is placed to the south-east of the *khara* mound.

Having strewn [the grass] upon it, he places the offering-ladles (srucaḥ) therein: 11. With the formula, "I yoke for thee the earth with light," he touches the *dhruvā* ladle; with "I yoke Vāyu with the intermediate space, together with that," the *upabhṛt*; with "I yoke speech with heaven, with the sun, together with that," the *juhū*; and with "I yoke the three openings of the sun for thee," all of them. 12. The vessels for Vāyu (*vāyavyāni*) are upright, a span in measure, with their centers joined together, and placed in the third layer. 13. With the formula, "Who yokes you? May He yoke you," [he places them] on the mound (*khara*).

He arranges the vessels: on the southern shoulder [of the altar] he places the *dadhigraha* vessel made of *udumbara* wood with four corners; on the northern shoulder, the two cups for the *upāṃśu* and *antaryāma* offerings; between those two, the *upāṃśusavana* pressing-stone. The other vessels for the dual-deity offerings are as follows: a wreath for the *aindravāyava* cup, the shoulder-blade of a goat for the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup, and a rib for the *āśvina* cup.

To the south and north are the *śukra* and *manthin* vessels made of *bilva* wood; the southern one belongs to the *śukra* and the northern one to the *manthin*. The two seasonal cups (*ṛtupātra*) are made of *aśvattha* wood with bases shaped like horse-hooves, similar to ladles (*sruk*) that are double-mouthed; of these two, the southern is the Adhvaryu’s cup and the northern is the Pratiprasthātṛ’s. On the southern hip of the altar is the *āgrayaṇa* vessel, on the northern hip the *ukthya* vessel and the *ukthya* cup, which has three prongs, a base shaped like a horse-hoof, and a front support. The *āditya* vessel and the *āditya* cup have eight prongs.

The *ṣoḍaśin* cup is made of *khadira* wood and has four corners. With the mantra, "O Vāyu, come hither; these Soma juices are prepared for you. Drink of them and hear our call," he worships the vessels dedicated to Vāyu. In front of the support of the northern *havirdhāna* cart, he places the *dhruva* vessel. Behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he places the *droṇakalaśa* with its handle intact; into it, he deposits the *pariplu* ladle and the *adaṇḍikā*.

And with two *daśāpavitra* filters made of white woolen threads, he prepares for the sacrificer a filter (*pavitra*) one cubit (*aratni*) long and a fringe (*daśā*) one span (*prādeśa*) long. 18. Below the northern [side], he sets out the *savanīya* jars: the largest jar for the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*) in the western half; the medium-sized one for the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*) in the eastern half; and the smallest one for the third pressing (*tārtīyasavana*). In an *agniṣṭoma*, the smallest is for the morning pressing; after the *ukthya*, the medium-sized; and the largest for the third pressing. The *ādhavanīya* jar is placed in the *nīḍa* (the interior of the cart).

In the front part [of the cart], he places the *pūtabhṛt* vessel. 19. On the southern support-beam, he sets down ten cups made of *nyagrodha* or *rohitaka* wood, of various forms, provided with handles. 20. With the formula, "I set you down, the slayers of Rakṣases, the slayers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu," he employs five pressing-stones (*grāvan*) on the pressing-skin; of these, the largest is the lower millstone (*upala*) placed in the middle, while the others face it. 21. Having lifted the King [Soma] over with a cloth, he lowers him onto the stones between the two poles with the formula, "For the heart thee! For the mind thee! 22. The sacrificer touches them with the *saptahotṛ* formula. 23.
When the night has dawned, before the utterance of speech, he begins the *prātaranuvāka* (morning litany).

He issues the commands: "Recite for the gods who come at dawn; O Brahman, restrain the speech; O Subrahmaṇya, invoke the Subrahmaṇyā; O Pratiprasthātṛ, pour out the grains for the *savanīya* offerings. Before the *vamśa*, the Pratiprasthātṛ pours out the grains for the *savanīya* offerings: for Indra accompanied by the Haris, barley-grains; for Indra accompanied by Pūṣan, groats (*karambha*); for Indra accompanied by Sarasvatī and Bharatī, parched grain (*parivāpa*); and for Indra, rice-grains for the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*). This cake is prepared on eight potsherds for the morning pressing.

The offering for the midday pressing is on eleven potsherds; that for the third pressing is on twelve potsherds. He prepares the *āmikṣā* with milk from one [cow]. There is no *payasyā* in the two subsequent pressings. [The procedure] is established up to the placing on the fire. While the grains are being roasted, he performs the *paryagni* rite. He grinds two portions of the parched grains (*dhānās*). When the verse "Dawn has appeared, bright-colored" is being recited, he offers with the *pracaraṇī* ladle, saying: "May Agni hear my call along with the fuel. Having taken [ghee] again into that same ladle, [he says]: "O Hotṛ, send forth the Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup-bearer."

"O Ekadhanins, lead up the wife; O Pratiprasthātṛ, having filled the Hotṛ’s cup with Vasatīvarī water, move it toward the south of the Hotṛ and wait at the edge of the Cātvāla pit," he commands. 9 They go up to the Cātvāla as directed. 10 "O Ekadhanins"—this is the call for the Savanīya jars. 11 The Pratiprasthātṛ, having filled the Hotṛ’s cup with Vasatīvarī water, moves it toward the south of the Hotṛ and [waits] at the edge of the Cātvāla.

"He desires [the fire]: 'Come, come! Let Agni lead you to the front; let Vāyu lead you to the middle; you are the young one released by the Rudras by name; homage be to you; do not harm me. With these words, the Neṣṭṛ leads the wife forward, her hand holding the water for washing. (12) At the place where he might overhear the Hotṛ reciting the morning litany (*prātaranuvāka*), there the Adhvaryu should take water from the flowing stream. (14) If it is far away, he should take it at the edge of the *cātvāla* pit. (15) Having thrown a blade of grass into the water, he offers an oblation over it with the formula: "O divine waters, O Son of Waters... (16)

Saying, "May you be capable," he causes the oblation to float with *darbha* blades. 17. Having placed *darbha* blades between [the vessels], he pours from the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup into the [other] cups against the stream, saying, "For the imperishability of the ocean, pour up. 18. In this same manner, [he proceeds] with the *savanīya* jars in successive order. 19. Having consecrated the foot-washing water silently with the formula, "Of the Vasus, of the Rudras," he hands it to the wife. 20. He pours the contents of the *maitrāvaruṇa* cups into the *hotṛ* cup over the *catvāla* pit. [He pours] those of the *hotṛ* cup [into the others].

21. With the formula, "May the yokes be joined with yokes according to their respective positions," he anoints the two cups belonging to the Maitrāvaruṇa with the *pracaraṇī* ladle. 22. Having entered the *sadas* by the western door, the wife, [the Adhvaryu] places the *pānnejana* water behind the *neṣṭrīya* seat, saying, "The Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas. 24. They lead the Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup, the Hotṛ’s cup, the *vasatīvarī* waters, and the *phalaka* fruits for the pressing in succession toward the *havirdhāna* shed, while the Hotṛ says, "O Adhvaryu, the waters have come down."

If someone asks, "Do you see this man? he should reply, "I see him. (25) In the Agniṣṭoma, he offers the *kratukaraṇī* oblation with the verse, "O Agni, that mortal in battles... (26) With this same [verse], one should anoint the enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) in the Ukthya; with this, the forehead-bond (*rarāṭī*) in the Ṣoḍaśin, or one should touch the *droṇakalaśa*. (27) Having placed the *pracaraṇī* ladle in the two *havirdhāna* carts, while muttering this [formula] at the front, he should enter the *havirdhāna*; this applies to the Atirātra, Vājapeya, and Aptoryāma sacrifices. (28) Into the Udumbara vessel provided with a filter, [he says]: "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati, thee!"

He draws the *dadhighraha* cup (29). It is offered while still close [to the fire] (30). He goes to the south of the *hotṛ* (31). Having approached from the north and stationed himself facing the southern junction of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), he makes an offering over it with the verse, "By which offspring are without gaps" (32). He worships it with the verse, "Three tongues of yours" (33). Having circumambulated, he places the vessel back in its proper place (34). Having poured out the *ādhavanīya* jar and having poured the contents of the *maitrāvaruṇa* cup into it, he pours in the morning-pressing portion (35) from the northern *havirdhāna* cart.

He places the Vasatīvarī waters below the southern axle-pole, and the two Savanīya jars to the north. Having placed the Hotṛ’s cup below the northernmost [of those], he makes the sacrificer recite over it: "The Nigrābhyās are present" (36).

With the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ," he takes the *upāṃśusavana* stone (1). Having consecrated it with the formula, "Thou art a pressing-stone" (grāvāsi), he restrains his speech (2). With the formula, "Be thou wide-open for King Soma; Indra, thee, the most exhilarating," he touches it with his hand holding gold (3). Having placed the *upāṃśusavana* stone upon the lower millstone (*upala*), he measures out the entire King Soma upon it five times with the formulas beginning, "Indra, thee, the slayer of enemies" (indrāya tvābhimātighne), according to the procedure at the purchase (kraya) (4). Having poured [milk] from the Hotṛ’s cup with the formula, "Ye are invigorating, O conquerors of Vṛtra," [he adds]: "O Soma, that which is thine... (5).

With the formula, "The light in heaven," he makes it possessed of a body by touching it. 5. The Pratiprasthātṛ, having removed a smaller half of the King’s garment, places it upon the black antelope skin. 6. "I have increased you with my mind, O well-born ones; born of the *ṛta*, may we be your fortune. O divine plants, being in agreement with Indra, grant us permission for the Soma-pressing."

Having thus handed over the King Soma, he causes the six shoots to swell two by two. 7. Having silently poured [water] from the Hotṛ’s cup, he lifts up the Upāṃśusavana stone while muttering: "Do not fear; do not tremble. 8. He consecrates the two pressing-boards with the formula: "O Dhiṣaṇās, you who are praised, be praised! 9. He consecrates that first shoot of the pressed juice which might fly away, saying: "Do not go away from me along with my offspring, along with my cattle, along with the increase of wealth; do not destroy my sensory power and my vigor."

He draws back [the Soma] and presses it upon the root. If he cannot find a root, he should place grass or wood underneath. Having pressed it eight times, he pours the third portion into the Upāṃśu vessel with his joined palms while reciting, "Flow pure for Vācaspati. In this same manner, having pressed it eleven times, and likewise twelve times. While the portions that have been set aside are being poured out, the Pratiprasthātṛ places two blades of *avaśū* grass between each pair. He mutters, "Make our offerings full of sweetness. Having taken [the cup] with the words, "Thou art self-made," he stands up.

"Go through the wide atmosphere," he says, and he proceeds. (16) He goes by the south of the Hotṛ's [station]. (17) Having approached from the north and having stationed himself facing the southern junction of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*), he offers with the formula, "To all the powers of Indra. (18) From where the offering has been made, he should wipe the vessel upwards: for one desiring rain, with the formula, "Thee for the gods who drink the rays of light," he should wipe upwards behind the middle enclosing stick; for one not desiring rain, he should wipe downwards inside the vessel, that is, he should wipe downwards inside the enclosing stick.

19. He pours the remnants from the *āgrayaṇa* vessel into it. 20. With the formula, "For breath thee," he sets down the *upāṃśu* cup; into it he places the *am̐śu* shoots. 21. With the formula, "That of thine, O Soma, which is invincible," the Pratiprasthātṛ releases two *am̐śu* shoots each into the *am̐śu* cups of those [cups] that have been drawn out. 22.

They sit down for the pressing: the Pratiprasthātṛ to the south of the pressing-stone, the sacrificer behind him, the Adhvaryu to the north, and the Unnetṛ in front. (1) Having silently poured water from the Hotṛ’s cup, they press with the stones. (2) Thereupon he undergoes the *nigrābha* rite. (3) He causes the pressed-out shoots to flow through the Hotṛ’s cup toward the east, west, south, and north. (4) Having squeezed them, he pours [the juice] back. (5) From this point upward, the Unnetṛ pours in the *vasatīvarī* waters. (6) They press. (7)

He undergoes the *nigrābha* rite again (8). Then he collects [the Soma] (9). Having pressed it, the *unnetṛ* pours it into the *ādhavanīya* jar and causes it to overflow (10). Then he milks [the cows] (11). Having poured the pressed juice into the *hotṛcamasa*, he pours from the full vessel into the one used for the morning pressing (12). Having pressed it, the *unnetṛ* pours it into the *adhiṣavaṇa* [skin] and sprinkles water upon it (13). They press [the Soma] (14). He undergoes the *nigrābha* rite four times.

He brings [the water] three times. (15) If he should undergo the *nigrābha* rite nine times, he undergoes the *nigrābha* three times starting from the secondary vessel (*upasarjana*) and brings [the water] together; he pours it out twice. (16) Thus is the second round, and likewise the third. (17) He strews the pressing-stones with the dregs (*ṛjīṣa*). (18) The Udgātṛ priest pushes forward the *droṇakalaśa* vessel toward the east; he throws away the *daśāpavitra* filter and the crossbar between the two axle-pins.

One should strike the axle of him whom one hates. With the formula "May the Vasus cleanse you," he cleanses the *droṇakalaśa* with the *daśā* at the morning pressing; with "May the Rudras cleanse you" at the midday pressing; and with "May the Ādityas cleanse you" at the third pressing. He places the *droṇakalaśa* upon the pressing-stones. Above it, the *udgātṛ*s spread out the *nābhi-pavitra*.

In that [cup], the sacrificer causes a continuous stream of Soma-juice to flow by means of the Hotṛ’s cup until the drawing of the Dhruva vessel. 21. The Unnetṛ pours [the juice] from the morning pressing into the Hotṛ’s cup. 22. He draws the cups from the stream of Soma-juice; for one who desires rain, he draws them with their mouths downward and full. 23. Having drawn them and wiped them with a fringed cloth, he places them in their respective positions. 24. "Thou art taken with a support; O Maghavan, restrain within"—with these words, he draws the Antaryāma cup. 25. It is offered while still remaining in its place. 26. He goes past the Hotṛ to the north. 27.

Having moved toward the southern [corner] and standing straight, he offers the northern cup at the joint of the enclosing sticks with the formula, "Vāk tvaṣṭu" (May Vāk fashion thee). 28. The wiping has been explained. 29. With "For out-breathing thee," he sets down the Antaryāma vessel like a cook. 30. With "For through-breathing thee," [he sets down] the Upāṃśusavana stone. 31. Once the sun has risen, he offers the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups. 32. But if he should be in a hurry, he may offer the Upāṃśu before sunrise.

After the Antaryāma cup, there are the foremost cups (grahāgrāṇi). If the Soma sacrifice has the Rathantara-sāman, one should draw the cups with the Aindravāyava as the first; if it has the Bṛhat-sāman, with the Śukra as the first; if it has the Jagat-sāman, with the Āgrayaṇa as the first. This order of the foremost cups is handed down in the text beginning with "He who is the eldest kinsman. He draws the Aindravāyava cup with the verse, "O Vāyu, come hither," using half the vessel; he completes the remainder with, "O Indra and Vāyu, these [juices] are pressed"; and he deposits it with, "This is your womb; for you two who are in harmony. Whatever other cup he might draw prior to the Aindravāyava, it belongs to Indra.

Having set down [the cup] for Vāyu, he should set that one down. (5) Having drawn the Maitrāvaruṇa cup with the formula, "This one for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa," he mixes it with warm milk; he sets it down with the formula, "This is your womb; for Ṛta and Ayu, you! (6) Having drawn the Śukra cup with the formula, "This one, the seer," he mixes it with gold; he sets it down with the formula, "This is your womb; for heroism, you! (7) Having drawn the Manthin cup with the formula, "Him as of old," while not making the vessels resound, he mixes it with groats; he sets it down with the formula, "This is your womb; for progeny, you! (8) Ya...

Having poured the Soma from the Āgrayaṇa vessel into the Hotṛ’s cup with the verse, "O gods who are eleven in heaven," he draws the Āgrayaṇa in two streams, consecrates it with, "Thou art the Āgrayaṇa, the good Āgrayaṇa," utters the *hiṅ* sound three times over it, releases his speech, and sets it down with, "This is thy womb; for the Viśve Devas thee. 9. With the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra the Bṛhadvat thee," he draws the Ukthya; he sets it down with, "This is thy womb; for Indra the [Bṛhadvat] thee. 10. [The Mūrdhanvan...]

He takes up the *dhruva* cup with the formula, "Thou art the day. Having consecrated it with, "Thou art firm, of firm abode," he deposits it with, "This is thy womb; for Vaiśvānara. For one who desires long life, he places it upon gold. The prince guards the *dhruva*. He should cause the *dhruva* to flow forth against whomsoever he hates. Having poured that Soma which belongs to the morning pressing into the *hotṛ*-cup, having strained it further, and having pressed the King [Soma], he places the filter beside it. Having poured from the *droṇakalaśa* into the *pūtabhṛt* using the dipping-spoon, he uses the fringe of the filter.

Having wiped [the vessels], he places them in their respective positions: 15. He touches the *droṇakalaśa* with the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati thee!"; the *ādhavanīya* with, "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra thee!"; and the *pūtabhṛt* with, "Thou art taken with a support; for the Viśve Devas thee! 16. With the verse, "The drop has fallen," he consecrates the drop that has fallen on all sides around the *droṇakalaśa*. 17. Having mentally recited the *Saptahotṛ* formula, he offers the oblation. 18. He issues the command: "O Prastotṛ, restrain thy voice! O Unnetṛ, cause the King [Soma] to flow together into the *ādhavanīya* vessel, facing eastward. 19.

From the *havirdhāna* shed, they proceed toward the *adhyāstāva* [platform] for the purpose of abandoning [the vessels]. The *prastotṛ* takes hold of the *adhvaryu*, the *udgātṛ* takes hold of the *prastotṛ*, the *pratihartṛ* takes hold of the *udgātṛ*, the *maitrāvaruṇa* takes hold of the *pratihartṛ*, the sacrificer (*yajamāna*) takes hold of the *maitrāvaruṇa*, and the *brahmā* takes hold of the sacrificer. With the two mantras, "May the mind, the light, increase; prosperity... and [the second], they silently offer the speckled butter (*pṛṣadājya*) that has been prepared. [The *hotṛ* recites: "May Speech go first, going straight ahead to the gods, bestowing glory upon me, vital breaths upon the cattle, and progeny upon me, the sacrificer."

The Adhvaryu creeps forward from the front, grasping a handful of *darbha* grass; having reached the *āstāva*, they sit down—the sacrificer following the left [side] of the Prastotṛ, and the Adhvaryu following the right. Handing the handful of *darbha* grass to the Prastotṛ, he introduces the chant with the words, "Soma purifies himself. The Adhvaryu shall not join in the singing. Prior to the *Bahiṣpavamāna*, the sacrificer mutters the *Daśahotṛ* formula and says, "For the sake of wealth, utter the *hiṅ*! and, "You are the falcon, having the *gāyatrī* metre; I take hold of you; lead me safely across."

And 8. While about to chant the praise, the Unnetṛ, having spread the filter over the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, pours in the contents of the *ādhavanīya*. 9. Having wiped it with the fringe, he places it face down in its proper place. 10. Whomever he may hate, he should exclude him from the *bahis-pavamāna* chant. 11. When the chant has been performed, he issues the command: "O Āgnīdh, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the cake-offering; O Pratiprasthātṛ, prepare the animal victim. 12. The Āgnīdhra, having taken embers from the *āgnīdhrīya* fire, distributes them among the hearths (*dhiṣṇya*) beginning with that of the Hotṛ, according to the order in which they were assigned, starting with the front ones.

Having entered by the Sāṃkāśana doors and having circumambulated the Hotrīya fire-altar on the north, he spreads a continuous line of *ulapa* grass from the *pṛṣṭhya-śaṅku* post over to the northern altar (*uttaravedi*). With the *pariplu* ladle, he draws a cup from the *droṇakalaśa* with the verse, "O Kaśā, that which is yours... He sets it down for the Aśvins with the formula, "This is thy womb; for the two Mādhvīs, thee! [He then recites: "O Viṣṇu, you who are our nearest, grant us protection and glory; your honey-dripping streams milk out an inexhaustible fountain."

Having thus touched the vessels with the verse addressed to Viṣṇu and having drawn out the cord, he winds the triple-cord around the sacrificial post and dedicates the animals: a goat for Agni in the Agniṣṭoma; a second, for Indra and Agni, in the Ukthya; a third, a ram for Indra, in the Ṣoḍaśin; and a fourth, a ewe for Sarasvatī, in the Atirātra. (15) This is established up to the Pravara. (16) Having taken eight pieces of fuel-wood, he chooses [the Hotṛ] with the calls for the seasons (*ṛtupraiṣa*) and so forth.

The Hotṛ, as prescribed; the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryus, from the office of the Adhvaryu—the Adhvaryu should whisper his own name and that of the Pratiprasthātṛ, and then loudly say, "The two humans. He throws a splinter of wood into the fire. The Agnīdh, from the office of the Āgnīdhra—the Āgnīdhra [does the same]. Mitrāvaruṇa, the two Praśāstṛs, from the office of the Praśāstṛ—the Praśāstṛ [does the same]. Indra, the Brahman, from the office of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin—the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin [does the same]. The Maruts, the Potṛs, from the office of the Potṛ—the Potṛ [does the same].

"O Gānavas, from the Neṣṭṛ [I choose] the Neṣṭṛ; thus [he chooses] the Neṣṭṛ. Agni is the leader of the divine clans, and this pressing sacrificer is the leader of men. May their household-fire shine for us so as not to be single-wheeled for a hundred winters. O two of you, may you join together in your bounty, yet remain separate in your bodies. Thus says the sacrificer. (17) "At every offering, may I become beloved of speech; Svāhā to Sarasvatī!"—with the dipping-spoon he offers thus a second time, and with a *ṛc* verse, "Fulfill the hymn of praise," a third time. (18) Not at the *savanīya*.

He subsequently prepares the sacrificial cake for Paśu. 19. This is established up to the offering of the omentum. 20. When the omentum has been offered, having performed the purification at the Cātvāla pit, the officiating priests and the sacrificer stand near the Dhiṣṇya hearths. 21.

At the appropriate intervals, the sacrificer looks at the cups: "O you two who bestow splendor upon me, purify yourselves through out-breath and in-breath," he says for the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma; "Purify yourself as the giver of splendor for my diffused breath," he says for the Upāṃśusavana; "Purify yourself as the giver of splendor for my speech," he says for the Aindravāyava; "Purify yourself as the giver of splendor for my skill and ritual action," he says for the Maitrāvaruṇa; "Purify yourself as the giver of splendor for my hearing," he says for the Āśvina; "O you two who bestow splendor upon me, purify yourselves for my two eyes," he says for the Śukra and Manthin.

"Granting splendor to my self, flow clear"—with this he [pours] the Āgrayaṇa; "Granting splendor to my limbs, flow clear"—the Ukthya; "Granting splendor to my life-span, flow clear"—the Dhruva. "Thou art the belly of Viṣṇu; granting splendor to me, flow clear for splendor"—the Droṇakalaśa; "Thou art the belly of Indra; granting splendor to me, flow clear for splendor"—the Ādhavanīya; "Thou art the belly of the All-gods; granting splendor to me, flow clear for splendor"—the Pūtabhṛt.

"Who are you? Which one are you? Or what is your name, you whom we have satisfied with Soma, you whom we have exhilarated with Soma? May you be rich in nourishment through nourishments, rich in heroes through heroes, rich in offspring through offspring, and rich in sight through sight—thus may I behold you. This [formula] is appended everywhere. "For brilliance, flow purifying, bestowing luster upon me"—this is for the clarified butter (*ājya*).

"Flowing for me, bestowing splendor upon the cattle, purify yourself"—with these words [he offers] the speckled butter; "May I attain that great longevity; may it protect me; by its name we cut off him who hates us and whom we hate"—with these words [he approaches] the oblation-holder (*havirdhāna*).

"May I attain the Vāmadevya, which is the life of all; may it protect me. By its name we cut off him who hates us and whom we hate. [He says this] at the Āgnīdhra fire. "Thou art the lord of life, the Rathantara; may I attain it; may it protect me. By its name we cut off him who hates us and whom we hate. Thou art the world; spread thyself! Homage to the seat! Homage to the Lord of the seat! To the seat!"

"Be firm, be unshakable, be well-disposed; O Heaven and Earth, protect me from distress; do not torment me, and do not move against me today or tomorrow"—thus [he addresses] the two door-posts. "Homage to the ancestors who dwelt aforetime, homage to those who dwell later! Come, O Soma-loving ancestors; may we be among those of yours who are mindful and unharmed. May we be good fathers through you; may you be rich in offspring through us. O Fathers! Ho! O Fathers! Ho! O Fathers! Ho!"—thus [he addresses] the southern half of the seat.

Beholding [him], they mutter: "Terrible are the seers; let there be homage today to them whose eye and whose ascetic heat are lofty and formidable. O Bṛhaspati, O mighty buffalo, O radiant one, homage, homage to Viśvakarman! May he protect us."

"Thus [he addresses] the Dhiṣṇya fires. (4) 'O divine Soma, may we dwell in prosperity through you, O Sun! May we honor you with the Gāyatrī for peace!'—thus [he addresses] the Āditya cup. (5) 'May Heaven and Earth call upon me; may the jars that hold the Soma, which are worthy of praise, call upon me; may the Hotṛ-offices call upon me in their invitation; the cows have been invited, and I am invited among the cows. (6) Having thus moved forward toward the Sadas while facing eastward, they sit down."

The sacrificer sits down to the south-east of the *hotrīya* hearth, and the two Adhvaryus sit to the north. The Pratiprasthātṛ, having spread a base of ghee in a vessel, sets out the *savanīya* offerings: the parched grains (*dhānā*) in the eastern half, the groats (*saktu*) mixed with curds or clarified butter in the southern half for the *karambha*, the groats in the western half for the *parivāpa*, and the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), having been heated, in the middle; the clotted curd (*āmikṣā*) in the northern half. Having thus adorned them and having taken portions into the *juhū* and *upabhṛt* ladles, [he offers] for Indra at every morning pressing.

Having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse for the *puroḍāśas* with the words, "Recite for the *puroḍāśas*"; then, having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he proceeds with the offering, saying, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the *puroḍāśas* of the morning pressing for Indra. 9. Having poured the butter from the *aupabhṛta* ladle into the *juhū*, he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse for the *puroḍāśas* for Agni with the words, "Recite for the *puroḍāśas* for Agni"; then, having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he proceeds with the offering, saying, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the *puroḍāśas* set forth for Agni. 10. Everything else is established as usual up to the removal of the potsherds, except for the *iḍā* invocation and the formal invitation (*upahava*). 11. Taking the two ladles or the cup belonging to Vāyu, he restrains his speech until the call, "Sacrifice! (*yajā*) is uttered. 12. At the *āgnīdhra* shed, the *āgnīdhra* priest stands with the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the sweeping-broom (*saṃmārjana*) in his hand.

Thereafter, standing upright upon the seat (āsandī), he responds with "astu śrauṣat. Once the response has been given, the Adhvaryu, having positioned himself facing the southern junction of the enclosing sticks (paridhi), offers oblations; the Pratiprasthātṛ offers in the northern part, while the Ājya-oblations, Puroḍāśa-oblations, and animal (paśu) oblations are offered in the middle of the fire, and the Soma-oblations on both sides.

The two [priests] proceed with the offerings for the dual deities. 1. The Pratiprasthātṛ offers the *pratinigrāhya* cups, which have been drawn, cup by cup, using the Āditya vessel. 2. He draws them with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu, thee! 3. Having taken the principal cup, the Adhvaryu [pours from] the Droṇakalaśa with the dipping-spoon, saying: "O Adhvaryu, let this sacrifice be for the gods, for the plants, for the cattle, and for my wealth! O gods, may it be firm for every being! Swell, thou who art rich in ghee, for the sacrifice to the gods, Svāhā!"

Thus he pours the *soma*-libation (*āghāra*). Having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he causes [the *hotṛ*] to recite, saying, "Recite for Vāyu and Indra-Vāyu! and then proceeds, saying, "Prompt for Vāyu and Indra-Vāyu! (5). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, the two offer the oblation (6). Having offered again at the second *vaṣaṭ*, they pour the remnants together (7). The *pratiprasthātṛ* pours everything from his cup into the *adhvaryu*'s cup (8). The *adhvaryu*, having poured the first portion of that [cup] into the *pratiprasthātṛ*'s cup, quickly brings the portion for consumption (9). He hands it to the *hotṛ*, saying, "This is Vasu, the one who possesses wealth in front" (10).

11. "Thou art taken with a support; for the gods thee!"—with these words, the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue from the Āditya-vessel into the Āditya-pot. 12. "Thou art taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa thee!"—with these words, he draws [the portion]. 13. Having taken the principal [portion], the Adhvaryu causes the Hotṛ to recite the invitatory formula according to the respective deity. 14. [The rite] is established up to the offering. 15. "This one is Vasu, the bestower of wealth"—with these words, he hands it to the Hotṛ. 16. "Thou art taken with a support; for the Viśvedevas thee!"—with these words, the Pratiprasthātṛ [pours the residue] from the Āditya-vessel into the Āditya-pot.

He pours out the residue. 16. With the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for the Aśvins, thee," he draws [the cup]. 17. Having taken the principal [cup], the Adhvaryu causes the Hotṛ to recite the invitatory verse according to the respective deity. 18. [The ritual proceeds] successfully until the offering. 19. He hands it to the Hotṛ with the formula, "This is Vasu; may he be united as Vasu. 20. With the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for the Viśve Devas, thee," the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue into the Āditya-vessel using the Āditya-cup. 21. [The procedure continues with] the revolving Droṇakalaśa.

With the words, "Of the sons of Diti," he fills the Āditya vessel from the *droṇakalaśa* with the *pariplu* ladle. (22) With the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee for Viṣṇu’s wide stride," he touches the Āditya vessel. (23) With the formula, "O Viṣṇu of the wide stride, this is thy Soma," the Pratiprasthātṛ covers the Āditya vessel with the Āditya cup; he covers it. (24) Thus ends the third chapter of the Mānava Śrautasūtra in the Agniṣṭoma.

At the end of the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, he places the *kāri-camasas* in the middle—those of the Hotṛ, the Brahman, the Udgātṛ, and the Sacrificer—and he draws out other *hotṛka-camasas*, with the exception of the *achāvāka-camasa*. He causes [the Āgnīdhra] to recite the invitatory verse for those being filled: "Recite for those being drawn out! O Unnetṛ, you draw out the *śukra* cups on both sides. Having made an under-layer from the *droṇakalaśa* and having tilted the mouths of the *pūtabhṛt* vessels, he fills them from the *droṇakalaśa*. With the formula, "Thou art Tutha, the supporter of people; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead thee forward," he takes the *śukra* cup.

"You are contented, O progenitor of people; may the gods lead you forth as the guardians of the knot"—with these words, the Pratiprasthātṛ [takes] the Manthin cup. (6) "The two, Śaṇḍa and Marka, have been driven away"—with these words, the two [cups] are set down. (7) They hold two chips of the sacrificial post underneath. (8) With two sprinkled chips of wood, they cover [the cups] with the formula: "O divine Soma, this is thy uncut portion. (9) They go out together with the two [cups] for taking. (10) "Join the life-force; join the breath; join the sight; join the hearing; join the mind. (11)

Saying, "Join the speech," they separate themselves behind the *uttaravedi* and join their hands and the two *graha* vessels. Saying, "Thou art unassailable," they step upon the *uttaravedi* with both thumbs, scratching the surface as they circumambulate the *uttaravedi*. The sacrificer touches it from behind. Saying, "May offspring be rich in heroes," the Adhvaryu [touches it] from the south.

With the verse, "May we have good offspring," the Pratiprasthātṛ stands to the north (14). With the formula, "Through Indra’s wrath," the sacrificer mutters (15). They both stand facing each other from the east (16). With the words, "Having come together," they join their little fingers (17). With the formula, "Thou art the support of the Śukra cup," he throws a splinter of the sacrificial fuel-wood into the fire (18). With the formula, "Thou art the support of the Manthin cup," the Pratiprasthātṛ [does the same]. With the formula, "Śaṇḍa is cast out," he throws a splinter of the sacrificial post outside the altar (19).

"The Marka has been cast out," says the Pratiprasthātṛ. 19. They proceed with the cups facing eastward; the two [officiants] proceed westward with the Śukra and Manthin vessels. 20. Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, the Adhvaryu says: "O Hotṛ, announce the pressed Soma-libations for Indra—those belonging to the morning pressing, accompanied by the Śukra and Manthin, dripping with sweetness—and say, 'Sacrifice! O Camasādhvaryus of the central performers, sacrifice at the *vaṣaṭ* and *anu-vaṣaṭ* calls! O Camasādhvaryus of the Hotṛ's assistants, having offered the cups once, fill them again from the Śukra vessel and return!"

He sends [the cup-bearers] forth (21); the cups are offered according to the order in which they were sent forth (22). Having recited the invitatory verses for the Śukra and Manthin cups (23), and having both recited the verse "That first preparation... (RV 8.92.24), the Adhvaryu offers the entire portion with the formula "To him, O Indra, the pressed [Soma]... (RV 8.92.25).

"To that Sūrya, offer the pressed [juice]," says the Pratiprasthātṛ; having offered thus, he offers the remainder in the eastern part of the northern half with "To the Rudras, svāhā! (24–25). He issues the command: "Let the Hotṛ’s cup go forward! Let the Brahman’s, let the Udgātṛ’s, let the Sacrificer’s go forward! (26). Having circumambulated, they set down the vessels in their respective places (27). He issues the commands for those who have been refilled: "One by one, having drawn [the portions], call for the *āśrāvaṇa* and say: 'O Praśāstṛ, sacrifice! O Brahman, sacrifice! O Potṛ, sacrifice! O Neṣṭṛ, sacrifice! O Agnīdh, sacrifice! (28).

Having offered at the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he distributes the portions for consumption (29). If the Hotṛ asks, "Has the Āgnīdhra sacrificed? he replies, "He has sacrificed" (30). They consume the Soma portions in the *sadas*; the *vaṣaṭ*-utterer, the one who performed the pressing and offering, and the *camasins* [consume them] after saying, "Invited, invite! or "Invited, invite yourselves! (31). Having consumed the portions belonging to the dual deities, the Hotṛ hands [the cup] over (32): "Consume! Come! Enter me! For long life and for well-being! Come, O Vasu, O Purovasu! Be dear and beneficial to me! May the Aśvins [protect] you! (33).

"I may attain through my two arms"—with these words he receives whatever the Hotṛ offers him. (33) "Thee, O divine Soma, who beholdest men, may I, with good sight, look upon thee"—with these words he gazes at it. (34) "Impel my limbs, O Lord of Bay Steeds; let not my groups thirst; as one auspicious, attend upon my seven seers; do not go below my navel. (35)

Thus, having restrained [the breath] in the vital airs while consuming the Aindravāyava cup twice (35), and having restrained [the breath] in the eyes without crossing over [the hands], they consume the Maitrāvaruṇa cup with the formula: "The mild, abundant, sacrificial banner, Vāc, delighting in Soma, may she drink" (36). Having restrained [the breath] in the ears while performing the circumambulation for the Āśvina cup from all sides, and having brought it back around, they consume it with the formula: "The mild, heavenly-speaking Aditi, whose head is uninjured, Vāc, delighting in Soma, may she drink" (37). He pours the residue from the Hotṛ's cup into [his own].

"Having eaten, having eaten—38. O King, do not cause us to tremble; do not strike my heart with hatred. Bestow vigorous strength upon me for long life and splendor. Having thus eaten each portion, he mutters this while beginning from the region of the heart. 39. Without placing it down, he should not release [the cup]; [he places] a piece of the *puroḍāśa* cake for Indra and Vāyu, the *payasyā* curds for Mitra and Varuṇa, and parched grains (*dhānā*) for the Aśvins. 40. Behind the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he sets down the vessels for the dual deities (*dvidevatya*). 41.

He cuts off the *avāntareḍā* for the *hotṛ*. (42) While it is being invoked, they lift up the cups without letting them touch one another. (43) Having lifted them together with the *hotṛ* and having invoked [the gods] together, they consume the cups with the formula: "O divine Soma, of thee who belongest to the Vasu-group, who knowest the mind, of the morning pressing, of the *gāyatrī* metre, offered to Agni, of Indra the *pota*, the honeyed—invoked, invoked—I consume. (44) "Be gracious to our heart when drunk, O Indu; O Soma, be very kind like a father to his son."

"Like a friend to friends, O wise one, with wide protection, do thou, O Soma, prolong our life for living. Having consumed each [portion] in this manner, he mutters [the verse] beginning from the region of the heart. (45) "Swell up; may thy milks unite," [with these words he consumes] the remnants of the portions. (46) Behind the axle of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, they set down the *nārāśamsa* cups. (47) The *achāvāka* priest sits down in front of his own hearth (*dhiṣṇya*), outside the *sadas*. (48) Having given him a piece of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), he causes him to recite: "O *achāvāka*, speak! (49) Upa...

When it is said, "O Brahmins, call upon the Brahmins," the Brahmin, desiring an invitation (*upahava*), says, "This one, O Hotṛ, invite! and [the Adhvaryu] gives the command. (50) He causes [the Maitrāvaruṇa] to recite the invitatory verse for the cup being lifted. (51) He draws the Achāvāka’s cup so that it is bright on both sides. (52) Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he gives the command: "O Achāvāka, sacrifice! (53) Having offered when the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ* have been uttered, he carries away the portion for consumption. (54) One should not consume from that [cup] together with anyone else; if one desires an invitation regarding it, one should say, "Consume! (55)

The consumption and the satiation have been explained. (56) Between [the two], he places the cup of the Neṣṭṛ and the cup of the Āgnīdhra for the Achāvāka. (57) They consume the *savanīya* offerings in the Āgnīdhra shed; they perform the purification rites either inside the altar or outside the altar. Or, having consumed them outside the altar, they perform the purification rites inside the altar. (58) He issues the command: "Satisfy the Brāhmaṇas at each pressing. (59)

They proceed with the seasonal cups (*ṛtugraha*). 1. The formulas for drawing the cups begin with "Thou art taken with a base; for Madhu thee! and so forth. 2. They draw the first two together. Having moved the *pariplava* spoon, the Adhvaryu [draws] with "For Madhu thee!"; the Pratiprasthātṛ [draws] with "Thou art taken with a base; thou art the uniter; for Aṃhaspatya thee! 3. Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, the Adhvaryu gives the command; at his command, they both offer simultaneously. 4. He does not perform the secondary *vaṣaṭ*-call (*anuvaṣaṭkṛti*) for the seasonal cups. 5. Having offered and drawn [the next cup], the Pratiprasthātṛ [proceeds].

Having moved toward the Adhvaryu from the south, he carries away the vessel. (6) They do not pass one another. (7) Regarding the remnant, they both grasp the northern part of the eastern [vessel]. (8) The Pratiprasthātṛ, being the first, takes [the portion] with "For Mādhava thee! Alternatingly with the subsequent [formulas]. (9) The position of the two when calling for the *āśrāvaṇa* is the same. They proceed with the six [formulas], beginning with "Prompted by the season (*ṛtu*)! (10)

Having taken from where it was offered into the vessel, he should offer with the four [verses] beginning with "Ṛtubhiḥ preṣya" (Prompt by the seasons); having likewise taken [the portions], he should offer with the two [verses] beginning with "Ṛtunā preṣya" (Prompt by the season). At the eleventh *praiṣa* (direction), when it is said, "O two Adhvaryus, sacrifice," one of the two, having sat down behind the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*), should sacrifice with: "Ye3 yajāmahe; may the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryus, drink the Soma through the season—*vauṣaṭ*! Or, if [he sacrifices] with a *ṛc*, he should sacrifice with: "Ye3 yajāmahe; O Aśvins, drink the honey, you who shine like fire and are pure in your vows, through the season."

"O you two who carry the sacrifice! Vauṣaṭ!"—thus he offers without pausing. (11) "O Hotṛ, recite the offering prayer for this!"—with these words he gives the *atipraiṣa* (extraordinary direction); at the final direction, either the sacrificer's *yājyā* (offering verse) or the *atipraiṣa* occurs. (12) Together they take the two final [cups]: the Pratiprasthātṛ with the formula "For Tapasyā thee," and the Adhvaryu with the *saṃsarpa* formula. (13) The Pratiprasthātṛ stands to the south.

At his command, they both offer simultaneously (14). Having offered, they pour out [the remnants] (15). The Adhvaryu pours everything into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel (16). The Pratiprasthātṛ, having poured the first portion of that [offering] into the Adhvaryu’s vessel with the verse, "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice," draws the draught for Indra and Agni into the Adhvaryu’s vessel; he deposits it with, "This is your womb; for Indra and Agni, you! (17). The Adhvaryu brings the portion for consumption from the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel (18). They consume it after inviting one another, saying, "May the goddess Vāc drink of the Soma."

19. As for the transposition of the offerings, he places the vessel down. 20. The Pratiprasthātṛ pours out the *savanīya* oblations. 21. Just as at the time of the commencement of the *vaiśvadeva* stotra, the call to the preparer of the oblation (*haviṣkṛt*) is made. 22. In front of the Hotṛ, facing eastward outside the *sadas*, he sits down to respond. 23. When it is said, "O Adhvaryu! Śoṃ! Sāvo! Om!", he turns around, saying, "Śoṃ! Sāvo! Daivo! 24. Grasping the *ṛtupātra* cup, standing upright in the *sadomaṇḍapa*, he [responds] with the Hotṛ in a uniform tone.

At the pauses, he responds with "Othā modaiva"; at those not preceded by a *praṇava*, with "Othā modaivo3m"; and likewise at the ends of the *ṛc*s. Or, just as the Hotṛ, when summoned, says "Śom̐ sāvo daivo3m," he responds. When the recitation (*śastra*) is completed, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup, and the Camasādhvaryus take up the cups. Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he issues the direction: "O Ukthaśās, sacrifice the Soma! At the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. The Camasādhvaryus lead the cups forward twice in succession. Vāgdevī [is] of the Soma.

"Let him drink"—thus [the Adhvaryu] says; they both consume the *sarvabhakṣa* (all-consumption) portion belonging to Indra and Agni. 31. "O divine Soma, of thee who art drunk by Narāśamsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the morning pressing, having the *gāyatrī* metre, and drunk by the Fathers"—thus the *bhakṣa-mantra* (consumption formula) is modified. 32. [The procedure] is established up to the placing [of the vessels]. 33. Having washed the *ṛtupātra* (seasonal cup) at the *mārjālīya* mound, he places it in its proper position. 34. With the verse, "The protectors, supporters of the people," he draws the *vaiśvadeva* cup into the *śukra-pātra*; with the formula, "This is thy womb; for the Viśve Devas thee," he sets it down. 35.

The Pratiprasthātṛ, having poured the Droṇakalaśa into the Pūtabhṛt and wiped it with the fringe of the cloth, turns it upside down in its proper place. (36) The sacrificer mutters the Caturhotṛ formula before the Ājya offerings and utters "hiṅ" for the Iḍā. (37) To the east of the Hotṛ’s seat, handing two blades of Darbha grass to the Prastotṛ, he says, "Come hither, O sacrificer," and thus introduces the Stotra. (38) In this same manner, he introduces the subsequent Stotras, except for the two Pavamāna chants. (39) When the word "eṣā" has been uttered, he sits down for the response.

That has been explained. (40) Having responded to the *prauga* recitation, the procedure is the same from the taking up of the cup until the consumption of the portion for Indra and Agni. (41) The mantra for consumption is modified to "of that drunk by Narāśamsa. (42) It is established [in its place] up to the setting down. (43) Having washed it at the *mārjālīya* fire, they set down the vessel at the end of the *pūtabhṛt* trough, each in its proper place. (44)

They proceed with the Ukthya portions in separate turns. 1. He draws [the third portion] from the Ukthya vessel with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee! He deposits it with the formula: "This is thy womb; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee! 2. He touches the Ukthya vessel with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the one who desires the gods, for the gods; thou art the oblation again. 3. From the Pūtabhṛt vessel, he pours out [the Soma] into the cups headed by the Maitrāvaruṇa cup. 4. The Stotra and Śastra take place. 5. Having responded to the Maitrāvaruṇa.

The Adhvaryu takes up the draught, and the Camasādhvaryus take up their cups. (6) Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he gives the direction: "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice the Soma-draughts! (7) He offers the oblation at the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ* calls, as do the Camasādhvaryus. (8) Having touched the *sadas*, he pours the residue from the Ukthya vessel into the Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup with the formula: "I fill thee, who art dear to the gods, for the gods. (9) They consume it with the formula: "May the goddess Speech drink of the Soma. (10) Having washed the cups at the Mārjālīya fire, they set them down in their respective places. (11)

The Pratiprasthātṛ proceeds with the next two [verses]. 12. With the formula, "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra thee," he draws [the Soma] from the Ukthya-vessel into the Ukthya-cup. 13. With the formula, "This is thy womb; for Indra thee," he sets it down. 14. In the same manner, he again makes it an offering. 15. From the Pūtabhṛt vessel, he pours out the cups for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the others. 16. There are the Stotra and the Śastra. 17. When the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin has recited his Śastra...

He pours the residue from that [vessel] into the cup (camasa). 17. The rest is the same. 18. He pours it out toward the pressing-rite (savana). 19. He places the *ṛjīṣa* on the black antelope skin. 20. With a cloth, he brings down King Soma onto the pressing-stones. 21. He pours the midday vessel into the Ādhavanīya jar. 22. "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra and Agni, thee!"—with these words, he draws the entire Ukthya-vessel from the Ukthya-pot.

"This is your womb; for Indra and Agni, you!"—with these words he deposits it. (23) He does not prepare the oblation again. (24) From the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, [he pours] everything into the cups headed by that of the Acchāvāka. (25) After the Acchāvāka has responded with the *pratigara*, the Adhvaryu should say, "O reciter of the *uktha*," and pours the residue into his cup. (26) The rest is the same. (27) Having filled the Hotṛ’s cup from the *vasatīvarī* waters, he deposits it in its proper place. (28) With the verse, "Agni [is the protector] from the morning pressing," he offers the *savanakarani* oblation, [reciting]: "That drop of thine which falls... and "That of thine which... and so forth.

"Flowing from the arm of the *śuṣ*, from the lap of the *dhiṣaṇā*, or from the *adhvaryu* or from the *pavitra*—that [soma] I offer to you with my mind, consecrated by the *vaṣaṭ* call. Thus is the second [offering]. 19. He gives the command: "O *praśāstṛ*, give the impulse! 30. Having been impelled, they move forward. 31.

They proceed for the midday pressing (mādhyaṃdina-savana). Having caused the sacrificer to recite, "The *nigrābhya* waters are present," he hands the Soma-wrapper to the Grāvastut priest and two garments to the Unnetṛ. Without being prompted, the Grāvastut recites the *grāvastotriya* verses. They press the King (Soma) after having brought him forth. The pressing has been explained. They press with the formula, "Hither! Hither! During the middle turn of the final round, they press with the formula, "Great! Great! This is established up to the stream of the *śukra* cup.

He draws the Śukra, the Manthin, and the others. Having poured that Soma which is in the Āgrayaṇa vessel into the Hotṛ’s cup from the Ādhavanīya jar with the dipping-spoon, he draws the Āgrayaṇa from three streams with the formula, "O gods who are eleven in heaven," while making a louder *hiṅ* sound. With the two Ṛtu-cups, they draw the two Marutvatīya libations. The Adhvaryu [draws] with, "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here," and the Pratiprasthātṛ with, "The fierce one has been born. He deposits them with, "This is thy womb; O Indra, who art accompanied by the Maruts."

Having drawn the Ukthya cup and having purified the King [Soma], he presses it; the procedure for the filter is established up until the *sarpaṇa* (creeping). 12. The Ṛjūdara priests creep forward for the midday pressing. 13. Having entered the Sadas by the eastern door to the north of the two *havirdhāna* sheds, they chant the Stotra in the Sadas. 14. Without overstepping the *dhiṣṇya* hearths, the Adhvaryu sits down. 15. The *saṃpāvana* (purification together) has been explained. Likewise is the introductory ritual (*upākaraṇa*) of the Pavamāna. 16. Before the midday Pavamāna, the sacrificer mutters the Pañcahotṛ formula and says, "Make the *hiṅ* sound for the light!"

"You are Suparṇa, having the Triṣṭubh metre; I take hold of you; lead me safely across," [with these words he steps forward]. 17. When the Stotra has been chanted, he gives the command: "O Āgnīdhra, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; prepare the sacrificial cake; O Pratiprasthātṛ, prepare the curds for the Dadhigharma. 18. The procedure for distributing the fires and the spreading of the ulaparājī-grass has already been explained. 19. Having touched the vessels with a verse addressed to Viṣṇu, they proceed with the Dadhigharma, provided that they perform the Pravargya rite. 20. From the removal of the Savanīya cakes onwards, the procedure is established up to the formal summons (saṃpraiṣa). 21.

The modified *saṃpraiṣa* (direction) is: "O Indra, [partake] of the sacrificial cakes of the midday pressing. (22) Having performed the rites with the *savanīya* offerings, he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse for those being drawn out, saying: "Recite for those being drawn out! (23) He draws out the cups belonging to the *achāvāka*. (24) [The procedure] is established up to the *saṃpraiṣa*. (25) The modified *saṃpraiṣa* is: "O Hotṛ, give the direction for the Soma juices set forth—the bright, the stirred, and the exclusive portion of the midday pressing belonging to Indra. (26) [The procedure] is established up to the *saṃyājana* (concluding offering). (27) The *achāvāka* is the first.

He offers from the Āgnīdhra fire. (28) Having lifted up [the cup] together with the Hotṛ and having invited [the gods], the modified *bhakṣa*-mantra is: "O divine Soma, you who belong to the troop of Rudras, who know the mind, who are for the midday pressing, whose metre is the Triṣṭubh, who are offered into the fire, and drunk by Indra. (29) [The rite] is established up to the placing [of the cups]. (30) They consume the *savanīya* cups at the Āgnīdhra fire; that has been explained. (31)

He offers the two *dākṣiṇa* oblations in the *śālāmukhīya* fire. Having tied a piece of gold with *darbha* grass, he places it into the butter taken in four ladlings. The procedure for covering [the fire] has been explained. Having brought the fringe of the garment near the handle of the offering-ladle, he makes the offering with the verse, "Upwards that Jātavedas... (RV 1.50.1).

He recites the second [verse], "The splendor of the gods... (RV 1.115.1). Having drawn [the butter] again during that [verse], he takes up the gold with the words, "Go to the sky! Go to heaven! (VS 10.23). While the [cows] stand facing the southern corner of the altar, he, holding both the gold and the clarified butter, approaches the sacrificial gifts (dakṣiṇās) with the formula, "I approach your form with my form" (VS 10.24). He distributes them with the words, "May Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you" (VS 10.25).

Up to those who share in the middle, half [of the fee] goes to the *ardhins*, a third to the *tṛtīyins*, and a fourth to the *pādins*. (7) The *brahmán*, *udgātṛ*, *hotṛ*, and *adhvaryu* are the *madhyataḥkārins*; their *ardhins* are the *brāhmaṇācchaṃsī*, *prastotṛ*, *maitrāvaruṇa*, and *pratiprasthātṛ*; the *tṛtīyins* are the *āgnīdhra*, *pratihartṛ*, *achāvāka*, and *neṣṭṛ*; and the *pādins* are the *potṛ*, *subrahmaṇya*, *grāvastut*, and *unnetṛ*. (8) He gives a goat, a sheep, beans, sesame seeds, prepared food, clothing, a horse, and gold.

The number of cows is one hundred and twelve, or unlimited, or at least twenty-one (9). From the latter half [of the herd], he leads the gold-handed Dakṣiṇā in front of the Gārhapatya fire and behind the Sadas (10). He consecrates the Āgnīdhra’s share with the verse, "This is thy gift, O Agni" (11). When the cows are stationed to the south, he offers an oblation on the Āgnīdhrīya fire with the verse, "May this Agni of ours... (RV 7.1.14).

"In the forests, the intermediate space"—with this he offers the second oblation; if it is a wheeled vehicle, [he offers] the third to Prajāpati; if it is an elephant or a man, [he offers] with "Go by the path of Truth. Between the *cātvāla* and the *āgnīdhra*, he releases them toward the north. Standing within the *vedī*, he gives the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) consisting of gold to the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*), beginning first with the *āgnīdhra*, saying: "Today may I be a Brahmin worthy of praise, possessing a father and grandfathers, a seer (*ṛṣi*) of seers' lineage, a possessor of a well-bestowed gift; this moon and these [other things] I give to you as the sacrificial fee."

Then, having led the *prāsarpaka* gift by way of the southern path from those who perform the middle [functions] down to the *hotṛkas* in sequence, and finally to the *pratihartṛ*, he should give it to the first among the *sadasyas*; then to the descendant of Atri; then gold. (14–15) Having entered the *sadas* with the mantra, "Open up the sky, look! (vi svaḥ paśya), he makes the sacrificer recite [the mantra]. (16) He consecrates the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇā*) with the mantra, "Our cows... (asmadrā tā). (17) He throws the black antelope horn into the *cātvāla* pit. (18) He does not give [gifts] after the two *marutvatīya* offerings. (19) To those to whom he would not have given here, he should give them once the omentum of the *anūbandhyā* cow has been offered. (20)

They proceed with the two Marutvatīya offerings. 1. He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse with the words, "Recite for Indra accompanied by the Maruts. 2. Having called for the Śrauṣaṭ, he proceeds with the offering, saying, "Prompt for Indra accompanied by the Maruts. 3. They both offer when the Vaṣaṭ-call is uttered. 4. Having offered again at the second Vaṣaṭ-call, they both pour out the remnants. 5. The Adhvaryu pours all [the remnant] into the Pratiprasthātṛ's vessel.

The Pratiprasthātṛ pours [the draught] from that [vessel] into the Adhvaryu’s cup. "Sajoṣā indre" (In harmony with Indra)—with these words, the Adhvaryu takes the Marutvatīya draught in his own cup and deposits it with, "This is thy womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, thee. The Adhvaryu brings the portion for consumption from the Pratiprasthātṛ. Having invited one another, they consume [it] with, "May the goddess Vāc drink of the Soma. He places the vessel on its support. The Pratiprasthātṛ pours out the sacrificial portions for the Savanīya offerings and the rice-pap for Soma. As...

At the time of commencing the *stotra* for the Māhendra cup, the *haviṣkṛt* call should be made. He sits down for the response (*pratigara*). This has been explained. Having responded to the *marutvatīya* recitation, the procedure is the same from the taking up of the cup until the consumption of the Aindrāgna cup. The mantra for the consumption is modified as follows: "O divine Soma, drunk by Narāśamsa, who knowest the mind, belonging to the midday pressing, having the Triṣṭubh metre, drunk by the Pitṛs. The rite is established up to the placing [of the cups]. With the verse "Great is Indra, manly," [he draws] into the Śukra vessel.

He draws the Māhendra cup with the formula, "This is for thee; O Mahendra, [that which is] thine. He deposits it with the formula, "This is thy womb; O Mahendra, [that which is] thine. This has been explained by the Vaiśvadeva rite; it is other than the Ukthya-vigraha cups, except for those belonging to the sacrificer. "Thou art taken with a support; O Indra, [that which is] thine"—thus the Ukthya is divided.

"This is your womb; for you, O Indra"—with these words he settles [the cup]. 19. The rest is the same. 20. He pours out the libation. 21. He throws the *ṛjīṣa* (the dregs) into the pressing-stones. 22. He pours the vessel belonging to the third pressing into the *ādhavanīya*. 23. From the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, he pours everything into the cups headed by that of the *achāvāka*. 24. When the *achāvāka* has responded, he should say: "The voice is united. 25. "May the All-gods, the Maruts, and Indra not abandon us at this second pressing."

"May we, speaking what is pleasing to these wise ones, be masters of riches. With this, he offers the *savanakarani* oblation. "O Indra, that drop which has fallen upon the earth—from the *parivāpa*, from the *puroḍāśa*, from the *karambha*, from the parched grains (*dhānā*), from the *soma*, from the *manthin*, or from the *śukra*—that I offer to you with my mind, accompanied by the *vaṣaṭ* call.
